title: Interlocks and permissives in Function Block Diagram: a guard that stops the motor
summary: Wire a permissive into the reset of an RS bistable so that the motor runs only while a guard is closed, and check it against the motor plant and its speed feedback.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence for a built-in motor plant model with one 10 ms task; they do not establish a safety function, guard wiring, stopping time, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Tell a permissive, a condition that must be TRUE for the output to be ON, from a command.
Wire the permissive into the reset of an RS bistable, which is reset dominant, so that an open guard drops the motor and also stops Start from restarting it.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/MotorPlant.fbd.json an RS block named Hold sets Command with Start and resets it with Stop, and an AND block sets Running when the plant reports AtSpeed. Add GuardClosed as a permissive: when the guard is open the reset must be TRUE, so that Command drops and Start cannot restart it.
stages.checkpoint: Command is ON only while the guard is closed, and Running still needs the plant's AtSpeed.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict Command and Running at {{t:30}} ms, when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms, and at {{t:60}} ms when Start is pressed with the guard still open.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:MotorPlant.Command=true,MotorPlant.Running=true@30|Both ON}} at {{t:30}} ms; {{v:MotorPlant.Command=false,MotorPlant.Running=false@50|both OFF}} at {{t:50}} ms; {{v:MotorPlant.Command=false@60|Command OFF}} at {{t:60}} ms, because Start is ignored.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter has no permissive on the guard, so when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms the motor keeps running and Start can restart it; reset the RS block whenever the guard is open. Place a NOT block on GuardClosed and an OR block with Stop and the output of the NOT block, then wire the OR output to Hold.R1 in place of the wire from Stop.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the motor plant answering your outputs.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named MotorInterlock and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:80}} ms: the motor is at speed at {{t:30}} ms, drops when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms, and does not restart at {{t:80}} ms when the guard closes, because Start was released.
stages.checkpoint: Command stays OFF from {{t:60}} to {{t:80}} ms and rises again only at {{t:90}} ms, with a new Start.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Why does the guard reach the reset of the RS block and not only Start? Put an AND block of Start and GuardClosed on S and leave R1 wired to Stop alone, and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: A permissive that gates only Start lets a running motor ignore an open guard. The scenario shows the logic only; it is not a safety function and does not replace a certified guard interlock.

hints.text: Command may be ON only if the guard is closed, Stop is not pressed, and either Start was pressed or Command was already ON. The RS block remembers the start, and its reset wins over its set.
Place a NOT block on GuardClosed, an OR block with Stop and the NOT output, and wire the OR output to Hold.R1. Leave Start on Hold.S.

faultCases: The starter has no permissive on the guard, so when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms the motor keeps running and Start can restart it; reset the RS block whenever the guard is open.
